The Poetry Chaikhana page was fetched: the whole sixteen line poem is there with the credit “from The Complete Poems of Anna Akhmatova, Edited by Roberta Reeder / Translated by Judith Hemschemeyer”, and the first stanza is the candidate word for word, with the comma after wisely, the comma after God, no comma after evening, and the full stop. A web search finds the same stanza credited to Hemschemeyer on several independent sites (Mindfulness Association, thomaswmorris.com, Goodreads quotes from the Zephyr volume). It is not the other widely circulated rendering (“I taught myself to live simply and wisely … to tire my superfluous worries”), which is a different translator, so the named translator and the wording belong together. The Zephyr volume itself was not opened (no open scan), so no page is cited and none is minted; that is the honest state. Facts check: Ya nauchilas prosto, mudro zhit is dated 1912 and was collected in Chetki (Rosary), 1914; Hemschemeyer’s Complete Poems first appeared from Zephyr in 1990 (two volumes, bilingual; expanded one volume edition 1992), so “1990” is right. The poem is untitled and identified by first line, as the source does. Poet’s own voice; no speaker needed. shipped.js: not shipped, nothing near, Akhmatova 0 of 3, not banned. In scope (1912; “pray to God” is a line of a lyric, not scripture); publishable; on theme as a daily practice. Source leads with the name, no dash, no straight quote, 117 characters. Tag Poetry correct. Minor: the source gives the poem’s date (1912) and the collection without its date; Rosary (1914) would be tidier and still fits.
